synthesis: Under the contradiction premise of a pole-free window, local denominator-zero counts permit selection of zero-separated Ingham lines, and logarithmic-derivative estimates turn that separation into quotient control on the horizontal boundaries. A decaying-kernel maximum-modulus step carries this control into a trimmed strip; a second, power-weighted kernel balances the vertical boundaries and transports an upper bound to a left line. The quoted mean-value theorem then converts goodness-supplied coefficient mass into a mean-square and hence pointwise lower bound on that same line, where comparison with the propagated upper bound rules out a sufficiently long pole-free window.
source_support: Lemmas 4.1-4.4 count zeros, select separated horizontal lines, and derive bounds for F2'/F2, F2^{-1}, and F. Lemmas 5.1-5.3 explicitly use kernel decay, two maximum-modulus rectangles, and vertical-boundary balancing to obtain the left-line upper bound. Step III applies the quoted Balasubramanian-Ramachandra theorem and goodness to force a large left-line value, and Step IV explicitly compares the two bounds to obtain the contradiction.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis composes a sequence of representation changes: discrete zero data becomes geometric contour clearance, logarithmic differentiation becomes multiplicative boundary control, kernel weighting becomes analytic transport, and coefficient nondegeneracy becomes a lower bound in the same left-line magnitude used by the analytic route. The contradiction becomes available only after both routes share that comparison currency.
limits: The zero-count and logarithmic-derivative estimates and the mean-value theorem are cited rather than proved here, and every stage remains conditional on the stated analytic, zero-free, numerator-growth, scale, and goodness hypotheses. Trimming loses parts of the height window. OCR damage makes exact regions, constants, powers, coefficient ranges, kernel normalizations, and the final numerical threshold unsafe without scan or cited-source verification.
quality_reason: Accepted because seven distinct parent units explicitly supply the linked contour-selection, boundary-control, two-stage transport, coefficient lower-bound, and final comparison mechanism; the relation is more informative than any parent alone and retains the proof burdens and extraction limits.

synthesis: The source separates two complementary inputs to its contradiction theorem. Its analytic hypotheses make a quotient controllable and, through a weighted maximum-modulus rectangle, yield an upper bound on a left vertical line. Goodness instead supplies recurrent coefficient nondegeneracy; in the later mean-square application that coefficient witness forces a non-small value on the same line. The pole conclusion needs their conjunction: analytic propagation alone supplies no lower obstruction, while goodness alone supplies no contour transport or pole conclusion.
source_support: The definition makes goodness a far-right convergence condition plus a coefficient-maximum lower bound at every sufficiently large scale. Theorem 2 places goodness beside continuation, boundedness, zero-free denominator, quotient, growth, and scale hypotheses before concluding a pole in the window. Lemma 5.3 constructs a power-weighted, decaying-kernel auxiliary function to propagate an upper bound to the left line, while Step III explicitly invokes goodness to lower-bound the left-line mean square and then its pointwise maximum.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis factorizes the theorem's assumptions by operational role and identifies the left-line magnitude as their interface: analytic data sets an upper envelope there, whereas coefficient data, mediated by a mean square, creates a lower witness there. This explains why neither hypothesis family substitutes for the other.
limits: The exact coefficient interval and exponent in goodness, the auxiliary-function normalization, rectangle scales, and all quantitative powers are extraction-damaged. The goodness-to-mean-square step also depends on the separately quoted Balasubramanian-Ramachandra theorem and its continuation, endpoint, and scale hypotheses. The result gives sufficient conditions and does not establish that either input is necessary in general.
quality_reason: Accepted because the definition, general theorem, analytic transport lemma, and coefficient application jointly support a concrete division of labor and shared comparison mechanism not stated by any one parent; the synthesis avoids treating goodness as a pole assertion or importing unsafe quantitative formulas.

synthesis: The base theorem is formulated for a good quotient built from shifted zeta factors, but the accompanying remarks relocate the proposed invariant from the Riemann zeta function itself to a constrained quotient architecture: derivatives and several ordinary, number-field, and ray-class L-function factors may be substituted, with a field-degree comparison replacing the original factor-count comparison. The concluding discussion broadens this into a provisional admissibility frontier that also requires denominator normalization and still lacks usable sufficient conditions for goodness; the stated forthcoming specialization shows one narrower shifted quotient where a distinguished pole implies recurrent high poles.
source_support: Theorem 1 gives pole recurrence for a good Dirichlet-polynomial times shifted-zeta quotient and for good finite sums. Remarks 1-5 explicitly list bounded-order derivatives, ordinary L-functions, arithmetic-progression series, number-field and ray-class zeta functions, a degree comparison, effectivity, and localized shifts. The concluding remarks label the broader product family as forthcoming, require a qualitative maximum-degree comparison and F2 tending to 1, and identify sufficient goodness criteria as unresolved. Theorem 3, attributed to forthcoming work, states recurrence for a purely imaginary-shift quotient under a distinguished-pole hypothesis.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis maps the base theorem's factor-count condition into a degree-based extension condition and organizes portability as separate obligations on quotient form, admissible factor families, denominator normalization, and coefficient goodness. It also distinguishes extensions asserted in remarks from the proposed frontier and the narrower forthcoming theorem, rather than collapsing them into one proved classification.
limits: The concluding maximal-family language is explicitly provisional, some results are deferred to paper IV, and the selected spans do not prove why the degree comparison licenses every substitution or provide the sought goodness criterion. Theorem 3 uses a distinguished-pole premise rather than stating the full goodness mechanism. Damaged product displays, indices, shifts, and inequality layout prevent exact factor reconstruction or a claim that the listed family is a proved maximal class.
quality_reason: Accepted at qualitative resolution because multiple sections concretely connect the original shifted-zeta quotient theorem to named replacement families and revised admissibility conditions, while the synthesis preserves the distinction between proved statements, extension remarks, and forthcoming-work claims and does not overstate the damaged formulas.
